title: Order of Subject Headings
summary: Governs the order of the subject headings assigned to a work (not the order of elements within a heading). The first heading represents the predominant topic and usually matches the class number; if two headings together express it, both go first. For individual biography the biographee's name is first. Two equally important topics follow each other before secondary headings, which may come in any order. LC does not use the 650 first indicator for primary/ secondary descriptors.
validation_rules: The first subject heading assigned represents the predominant topic of the work (usually corresponding to the class number). (H 80 sec. 1)
If the predominant topic needs two headings, they are assigned first and second, in either order (the one closer to the class number usually first). (H 80 sec. 1)
For individual biography, the first subject heading is the name of the biographee. (H 80 sec. 1)
For two equally important topics, headings for the second follow immediately after those for the first, before secondary topics. (H 80 sec. 2)
Headings for secondary topics and those completing standard arrays may follow in any order. (H 80 sec. 3)
[LC practice] LC does not use the 650 first indicator to mark primary/secondary descriptors. (H 80 Background note)

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text:
Assign the heading that represents the predominant topic of the work as the first subject heading.

If the predominant topic cannot be represented by a single heading, assign as the first and second headings the two headings that, taken together, express the predominant topic. Although it is not significant which of the two is assigned first and which second, if one of the two more closely approximates the class number it is usually assigned first.

For works of individual biography, assign as the first subject heading the name of the biographee.

sections.heading: 2. Works with two equally important topics
sections.text: If a work has two equally important major topics, assign heading(s) for the second of these topics immediately after the heading(s) for the first, and before any headings for secondary topics.

sections.heading: 3. Order of secondary topics
sections.text: Assign headings for secondary topics, as well as headings required to complete standard arrays, in any order following the heading(s) for the major topic(s).
